home.stat3Label: Executive Committee members driving the mission

about.title: About FCIAZ
about.subtitle: A national association born from a clear conviction: no woman in Zambia should lose her dignity to a preventable childbirth injury.
about.historyBody: FCIAZ was founded in 2026 by a group of Zambian clinicians, surgeons, and public health leaders who saw that obstetric fistula and related childbirth injuries — though preventable and treatable — continued to affect thousands of women, often in silence. The association was created to give the issue a national voice, and to coordinate the actors best placed to respond: government, professional societies, teaching hospitals, cooperating partners, civil society, and affected communities themselves.
about.missionBody: To become Zambia's leading voice in eliminating preventable obstetric fistula and childbirth injuries through advocacy, partnerships, education, quality treatment, reintegration, and research.
about.visionBody: A Zambia where no woman suffers preventable injury from childbirth, and every survivor receives the care, dignity, and opportunity she deserves.
about.valuesSubheading: Five principles guide every FCIAZ decision.
about.valueDignityDescription: We centre the voices, choices, and privacy of survivors in everything we do.
about.valueIntegrityDescription: Transparent governance, accountable use of resources, and honest partnerships.
about.valueEquityDescription: Reaching women in rural and underserved areas, regardless of background or ability to pay.
about.valueEvidenceDescription: Programmes grounded in clinical practice, public health research, and what works.
about.valuePartnershipDescription: We work with — not alongside — government, professional bodies, and communities.
about.boardSubheading: Elected members guiding FCIAZ during its foundational year.
about.registrationBody: FCIAZ is being registered under the NGO Act of Zambia. Registration with the Registrar of Societies, the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA), and PACRA is in progress. Once complete, the association will operate the official bank account through which all donations and grants will be received.

whatWeDo.title: What we do
whatWeDo.subtitle: FCIAZ works across three interconnected programmes. Each one is needed — none alone is sufficient.
whatWeDo.advocacyTagline: Making maternal health a national priority.
whatWeDo.advocacyBody: We engage government, media, professional bodies, traditional leaders, churches, and civil society to keep obstetric fistula and childbirth injuries on Zambia's health agenda.
whatWeDo.advocacyPoint1: National awareness campaigns aligned with key dates such as the International Day to End Obstetric Fistula (23 May).
whatWeDo.advocacyPoint2: Stakeholder courtesy visits to the Ministry of Health, teaching hospitals, OGSZ, the Medical and Nursing Councils, and cooperating partners.
whatWeDo.advocacyPoint3: Evidence-based policy briefs, press releases, and a national media kit.
whatWeDo.advocacyPoint4: Community sensitisation with traditional leaders, churches, and women's groups.
whatWeDo.treatmentTagline: Connecting women to quality, dignified care.
whatWeDo.treatmentBody: We work alongside clinicians and teaching hospitals to expand access to timely surgical repair and post-operative care.
whatWeDo.treatmentPoint1: Referral pathways linking survivors to fistula repair services at UTH Women and Newborn Hospital and partner centres.
whatWeDo.treatmentPoint2: Clinical training, mentorship, and continuous professional development for surgeons, nurses, and anaesthetists.
whatWeDo.treatmentPoint3: Quality assurance, audits, and patient outcome monitoring.
whatWeDo.treatmentPoint4: Equipping treatment centres with consumables, instruments, and supplies.
whatWeDo.integrationBody: Reintegration is the bridge from surgery back to a full life. We partner with physiotherapists, counsellors, and social workers to support reintegration.
whatWeDo.integrationPoint1: Physiotherapy and pelvic floor reintegration programmes.
whatWeDo.integrationPoint2: Psychosocial counselling for survivors and their families.
whatWeDo.integrationPoint3: Economic empowerment through skills training and micro-enterprise support.
whatWeDo.integrationPoint4: Peer support groups, including the Faces of Hope Campaign.
whatWeDo.researchTagline: Learning what works and sharing it.
whatWeDo.researchBody: We collaborate with universities and researchers to generate evidence on prevention, treatment outcomes, and survivor experiences in Zambia.
whatWeDo.researchPoint1: Partnerships with Levy Mwanawasa Medical University, UNZA, and Copperbelt University.
whatWeDo.researchPoint2: Annual scientific symposia and clinical updates.
whatWeDo.researchPoint3: Surveillance and outcome data shared with the Ministry of Health.

getInvolved.title: Get involved
getInvolved.subtitle: There are many ways to support FCIAZ — at home, in your community, or through your organisation.
getInvolved.donateBody: Your contribution funds awareness campaigns, surgical supplies, training, and reintegration programmes for survivors.
getInvolved.volunteerBody: Volunteers support events, translations, community outreach, photography, and professional services. Tell us your skills and availability.
getInvolved.partnerBody: We welcome partnerships with NGOs, hospitals, professional bodies, universities, media houses, and corporate Zambia.
getInvolved.advocateBody: Share our content on social media, host a community talk, or distribute educational materials in your network.
getInvolved.campaignFacesBody: Restoring dignity to women living with fistula through survivor stories (with informed consent), educational videos, myth-busting facts, and reintegration success stories.
getInvolved.campaignDayTitle: International Day to End Obstetric Fistula — 23 May
getInvolved.campaignDayBody: Each year on 23 May, FCIAZ joins the global community in raising awareness. Watch this space for events, school outreach, and media coverage.
